origin_port: proprietor, carrying on business at Gloucester.
cargo: This debtor came up at the Gloucester Bankruptcy Court for a first examination. The unsecured liabilities amounted to £1,698 10s. 10d., and the assets were estimated by the bankrupt at £606 5s. 6d., or, having regard to the realisation so far, a little over £400. He had previously failed in 1881, when his liabilities were over £16,000. Since that time he had gradually rebuilt up a large business, but a fire last year, and several bad debts brought about his failure. It appeared that the debtor commenced business about eight years ago without any capital of his own, and he has done a large business in contracts for the Great Eastern Railway Company over their system, but latterly, in consequence of keener competition, this business has fallen off considerably, and some two years ago he embarked in the cycle trade, he being a well known rider, and during the last two years he has acted as handicapper for the local Cyclists Union in that district. He alleged his failure to have been caused through insufficient capital and losses by bad debts. He had no offer of composition to submit to the meeting. Adnett, of Peterborough, be appointed trustees to wind up the estate under the deed, in conjunction with a committee of inspection consisting of five of the largest creditors.

cargo: The first meeting of creditors in this case was held at the London Bankruptcy Court, on Monday, before Mr. A. H. Wildy, Official Receiver. The accounts showed unsecured debts £652 12s. 1d., and debts fully secured £709 10s. 10d. against assets £196 4s. 2d. The debtor commenced business in September, 1894, with £45 capital. He attributes his failure to losses under a contract through increase in the price of building materials and to alleged illegal possession taken by the freeholder, also to bad debts, and to his inability to obtain tenants for houses that he had completed. In the absence of a quorum of creditors the meeting was adjourned for a week.

raw_line: About half-past twelve on Tuesday morning the Glasgow Fire Brigade were called to an out-break of fire on the premises of Andrew Campbell & Co., boatbuilders, Springfield Quay. Detachments from the Central and South, under Firemaster Paterson, were promptly on the scene, but the building was well alight before their arrival. Before the fire was checked considerable damage was done to the upper floors of the building, and to the saw-mill on the ground floor. The loss is estimated at from £1,000 to £1,200. The building is of brick, three storeys in height, and measures 90 ft. by 40 ft.

origin_port: An application was made, at the Hanley Bankruptcy Court, last week, before his Honour Judge Jordan, for the discharge of the above
cargo: named bankrupt. It appeared from the Official Receiver's report that the receiving order was made on January 18th, 1897, on the debtor's own petition. He filed a statement of affairs under the proceedings, showing liabilities expected to rank for dividend amounting to £984 8s. 6d., but the proofs admitted amounted to £1,115 8s. 7d. The Official Receiver pointed out that the bankrupt's assets were not of a value equal to 10s. in the pound, and that he omitted to keep proper books of account. His Honour granted the bankrupt an immediate order of discharge, provided judgment was entered against him for £10, to augment the dividend paid to the unsecured creditors. He also granted a certificate to the effect that the bankruptcy had been brought about by misfortune, and not by any misconduct on the part of the debtor.

origin_port: The sitting for the adjourned public examination of this bankrupt was held at the Kingston
raw_line: Thames. -The sitting for the adjourned public examination of this bankrupt was held at the Kingston-on-Thames Bankruptcy Court on Tuesday, before Mr. Deputy-Registrar Bell. The accounts filed disclose gross liabilities £5,758 0s. 8d., of which £2,825 19s. 1d. is expected to rank for dividend, and assets estimated to produce £143 15s. 4d. The failure was alleged by the debtor to be "Loss on contracts, speculative building, alteration and improvements, bad debts, want of premises, and ill-health." The Bankrupt failed to attend, but it was stated a telegram had been received from him stating that he was too ill to make the journey. Mr. Britten, assistant Official Receiver, explained that he should have to apply for an adjournment, as the bankrupt had failed to comply with an order served upon him by the Official Receiver for accounts. A solicitor appearing on behalf of creditors stated that he could not oppose an adjournment under the circumstances, and the Deputy Registrar adjourned the examination until the 31st inst., and made an order that the plaintiff should furnish the accounts required by the Official Receiver within ten days.

JONES, JAMES PRICE, builder and contractor, Mount Pleasant, Abercynon.—The statutory meeting of the creditors interested under the failure of James Price Jones, took place at the offices of the Official Receiver, Merthyr, on Thursday last week. It appeared from the statement of affairs filed by the debtor, that there were 39 unsecured creditors, with liabilities amounting to £360 8s. 8d., and two creditors fully secured for £640. The securities in the hands of fully secured creditors were estimated to realise a surplus of £160.
